summary: The design fits the repository’s storage abstraction, but the accepted scope leaves important lifecycle, pagination, path, and HTTP-serving contracts underspecified. The highest risks are reusing O365 authentication through the current toolkit flow and adapting stateful SharePoint resolution into a concurrent manager.

suggestions.title: Define an authenticated-client injection boundary
suggestions.rationale: `O365Tool._get_client` creates and caches a generic `O365Client`, while the proposed managers compose `SharepointClient` or `OneDriveClient`, whose drive-resolution and upload helpers live on those subclasses. If each manager creates its own client, delegated/OBO authentication, token caching, and cleanup will be duplicated or bypassed; if it accepts the generic client, the required backend helpers are unavailable. Add an explicit backend-client/factory injection path and make the toolkit refactor authenticate exactly once.

suggestions.title: Remove SharePoint site resolution’s hidden mutable input
Keep sharing-link options off the exact interface method
suggestions.rationale: The navigator contract defines `get_file_url(self, path, expiry=3600)`, while the proposal adds `scope` and `link_type` to that method. If signature fidelity is required, expose a separate `create_sharing_link(path, *, scope, link_type, expiry)` extension and keep `get_file_url` as the compatibility wrapper with constructor defaults. This also makes the side effect of creating a Graph sharing link explicit.

suggestions.title: Implement pagination for every list and search operation
suggestions.rationale: The existing SharePoint and OneDrive tools call `.children.get()` and Graph search once, so large drives silently return only the first page. Delta already treats continuation links as a first-class concern. The manager must follow `@odata.nextLink` for children and search, apply filters across all pages, and apply `max_results` after filtering.

suggestions.title: Use one bounded retry policy for SDK and raw HTTP paths
suggestions.rationale: The proposal relies partly on Kiota retry middleware, but upload chunks and copy/download polling use raw `aiohttp` paths. Existing upload code only handles `Retry-After` on a successful `202`, while the delta helper already contains reusable status/header parsing. Centralize retry-after parsing, attempt limits, delay caps, and 429/503/504 handling; avoid blindly retrying non-idempotent operations such as copy submission.

suggestions.title: Validate copy-monitor URLs before sending credentials
suggestions.rationale: Graph copy is asynchronous, so polling a server-provided monitor URL with `aiohttp` creates an outbound-request and bearer-token boundary absent from the current clients. Validate scheme, host, drive/job scope, and redirect behavior before polling; do not log the URL or forward credentials to an untrusted origin. The delta-link validator provides an established security pattern for structural Graph URL validation.

suggestions.title: Do not claim streaming while using the existing serving extension unchanged
suggestions.rationale: `FileServingExtension` downloads the entire remote object into `BytesIO` for both full responses and range responses. A Graph-backed manager would therefore buffer potentially large files in memory, and range requests would still fetch the whole object. Either add a remote streaming/range implementation or document and enforce a size limit before registering `setup()`.

suggestions.title: Specify path and folder semantics separately from legacy tool paths
suggestions.rationale: `FileManagerInterface` describes `list_files` as listing files, but the existing O365 list tools return folders and files together; `FileMetadata` has no folder flag. SharePoint legacy paths include a library segment, while the proposed manager path is drive-relative and the OneDrive tools use arbitrary path prefixes. Define whether folders are excluded from `list_files`, how `prefix` is stripped, and how legacy response paths map to manager paths before refactoring the tools.

suggestions.title: Make OneDrive user targeting cache-safe
suggestions.rationale: `OneDriveClient` currently caches one `_drive_info` and `_drive_id`, and `_resolve_drive()` always targets `me`. Adding user targeting to that mutable client can return a previously resolved user’s drive when a manager is reused or concurrent operations change the target. Resolve by an immutable user key and cache per user/authentication context, or keep user resolution entirely in the manager.

suggestions.title: Test batch result and cancellation semantics explicitly
suggestions.rationale: The brief says batches never raise, while the edge cases also describe aborting remaining work after authentication failure. Define a Pydantic result with explicit `succeeded`, `failed`, and `skipped/aborted` states, item identity, attempt count, and normalized error code. Test input-order preservation, duplicate destinations, partial auth failure, cancellation propagation, and a shared `BinaryIO` being rejected or copied safely.

suggestions.title: Preserve lazy-import and optional-dependency guarantees
suggestions.rationale: The existing file shim tests that importing `parrot.interfaces.file` does not load cloud SDKs, while `msgraph-sdk` and Azure authentication are listed in the `agents` extra rather than the core dependency set. Add lazy-import tests for both new managers and either create a dedicated `ai-parrot[msgraph]` extra or clearly make the manager unavailable without that extra; otherwise factory discovery will fail in otherwise valid core installations.
